demonstration_summary.title: ${var.title} complete
demonstration_summary.summary: The walkthrough selected ${var.service} for “${scenario.title}”, followed a representative trace through ${truth.scope}, and inspected the detail that explains ${truth.finding}.

checks.title: Service context
checks.detail: The ${var.service} APM service was selected so unrelated services could not distort its RED metrics.

checks.title: Trace path
checks.detail: A representative trace made the affected path ${truth.scope} visible end to end.

checks.title: Decisive detail
checks.detail: A span, error, dependency, or correlated log corroborated ${truth.finding}.

demonstration_summary.evidence: The service metrics, trace topology, and decisive detail support this conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

answer.evidence: The representative APM trace connects ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Select the affected service context
goals.concept: APM service and environment filters define the RED metrics and samples being compared.
goals.narration: Open the affected service in the run environment.
goals.reasoning: Service context prevents unrelated traces from entering the comparison.
goals.evidence: The service page shows scenario transactions.

demonstration.narration: Open the ${var.service} service in APM for “${scenario.title}”. This puts its latency, throughput, failure rate, and transaction samples in view before we follow a single request.
demonstration.reasoning: The APM inventory combines many services. Selecting ${var.service} prevents unrelated traces from entering the comparison and gives us the correct service-level context for ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The service page should now show transactions from this scenario. This establishes where to investigate; it does not yet prove ${truth.finding} or explain the full conclusion.

hints: Start from the service involved in the reported request.
Select ${var.service}; Show me can navigate there.

goals.title: Open the affected transaction group
goals.concept: Transaction groups aggregate requests with the same operation so their latency and failure distribution can be compared.
goals.reasoning: The group connects the service-level symptom to representative request samples.
goals.evidence: The transaction detail view shows samples for the affected operation.

demonstration.narration: Open the transaction group associated with ${truth.scope}. A transaction group collects requests that performed the same operation, letting us move from the broad ${var.service} service page to comparable request samples.
demonstration.reasoning: Service-wide metrics tell us there is a symptom but can combine unrelated operations. The transaction group narrows the question to the operation where ${truth.finding} should be visible.
demonstration.evidence: The transaction detail view should show the latency or failure distribution and sample requests for ${truth.scope}. Those samples give us candidates for checking ${truth.finding} end to end.

hints: Use the transaction table on the service overview.
Open the operation with the scenario latency or failures.
Select the affected transaction group; Show me can open it.

goals.title: Open a representative trace
goals.concept: A trace reconstructs one end-to-end request across transactions and spans.
goals.reasoning: The trace makes timing and propagation relationships explicit.
goals.evidence: The representative trace contains the scenario signal.

demonstration.narration: Choose one representative trace sample from the affected transaction group. The trace will reconstruct a single request across every participating service and span in ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.reasoning: Aggregated percentiles and error rates cannot show where time was spent or how failure propagated. A trace makes the ordering and duration of each operation explicit so we can locate ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.evidence: The trace waterfall should contain the scenario signal along the ${truth.scope} path. We expect its timing or repeated/error spans to make ${truth.finding} visible before opening the decisive detail.

hints: Move from the transaction group to one request.
Choose a representative sample; Show me can demonstrate it.

goals.title: Inspect the decisive trace detail
goals.concept: Span, error, dependency, and correlated-log details explain where the symptom originated.
goals.narration: Inspect the relevant trace element and its context.
goals.reasoning: The decisive detail distinguishes origin from upstream impact.
goals.evidence: The selected detail corroborates the finding.

demonstration.narration: Open ${var.inspect_label} on the representative trace and inspect its context. We are looking for the span, error, dependency, or correlated record that directly corroborates ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: A slow or failed upstream transaction can be impact rather than origin. The deepest decisive detail tells us which operation introduced the problem and which services merely inherited it along ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The selected detail should corroborate the trace-level signal and explain why ${truth.finding} occurred. Together, the topology and detail support the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Follow the slow or failed path to its deepest decisive element.
Inspect a span, error marker, or correlated log.
Use ${var.inspect_label}; Show me can open it.

goals.title: Submit a trace-supported conclusion
goals.concept: Separate the originating operation from the services where its impact becomes visible.
goals.narration: Record the finding, scope, and trace evidence.
goals.reasoning: A trace-backed conclusion should identify both cause and propagation.
goals.evidence: The answer cites the representative path and detail.
hints: State where the issue starts and how it affects the request.
Include finding, scope, conclusion, and evidence references.
